cards.b: Weather is short-term conditions; climate is the average over at least 30 years.
Measures wind speed in km/h or m/s, in an open site about 10 m up.
Shows wind direction, named by where the wind comes FROM.
Funnel and cylinder in an open site; measures rainfall in mm, read at the same time daily.
Unit of cloud cover: eighths of the sky covered, 0 to 8.
Measure humidity: a bigger difference between them means drier air.
Let air flow through but keep out direct sun and rain.
Avoids heat given off by the ground.
About 26–28 °C all year, annual range only 1–3 °C.
Over 2000 mm, all months, mostly afternoon convectional storms.

cards.f: Why is the equator hot all year?
cards.b: The sun is high (nearly overhead) all year, giving strong concentrated heating.
Under 250 mm a year, unreliable, often in flash-flood storms.

cards.f: Why do hot deserts have big day-night ranges?
cards.b: Cloudless skies: strong heating by day, heat escapes quickly at night.

cards.f: Why is it dry in hot deserts?
cards.b: Air sinks under high pressure, warms and forms no cloud.

gaps.s: The average weather over at least 30 years is called ___.
Wind direction is shown by a wind ___.
The Stevenson screen is painted ___ to reflect sunlight.
Rainfall in the equatorial climate is mainly ___ rainfall.
Hot deserts lie under zones of ___ pressure.
Air pressure is measured with a ___.
Hot deserts receive less than ___ mm of rain a year.

short.q: Describe how a rain gauge is used to measure rainfall.
short.model: It is set in an open space away from trees and buildings, with the funnel top level and above the ground to avoid splash. Rain collects in the cylinder and is read in mm at the same time each day.
points: sited in the open, away from obstacles
read in mm at the same time each day

short.q: Explain why temperatures in the equatorial climate vary very little through the year.
short.model: The sun is high in the sky all year so heating is constant. Day length is also about 12 hours all year and cloud limits night cooling.
points: constant heating, no seasons (day length similar)

short.q: Explain why hot deserts are very cold at night.
short.model: The skies are cloudless and the air is dry, so the heat gained in the day escapes quickly into the atmosphere after sunset.
points: no cloud cover to trap heat
heat escapes quickly / dry air holds little heat

short.model: The sun heats the ground, which heats the air so it rises. The rising air cools, its water vapour condenses into cloud, and heavy rain falls.
points: cools and condenses to cloud then rain

short.q: State two differences between the climates of the equator and a hot desert.
short.model: The equator has over 2000 mm rain all year, hot deserts under 250 mm. The equator has a tiny annual range of 1–3 °C, deserts have a much larger daily and annual range.
